aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.prompt: After a layoff, a 41-year-old has daily anhedonia, insomnia, guilt, low energy, and poor concentration for 18 days. There is no two-year history of low mood. What is the best DSM-5-TR diagnosis for the LCSW to consider?

options.a: Major depressive disorder, single episode, given a two-week-plus syndrome without chronic dysthymic course
options.b: Persistent depressive disorder, because any job-related low mood lasting more than two weeks is called dysthymia
options.c: Adjustment disorder only, because a layoff is present so a full major depressive episode is excluded
options.d: Cyclothymic disorder, because first-onset adult depression always implies undetected hypomanic cycling

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.explanation: A major depressive episode needs five or more symptoms, including depressed mood or anhedonia, most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks, with distress or impairment. This client meets that count and duration after a stressor, without a two-year low-mood history that would support persistent depressive disorder. A precipitant does not bar MDD when full MDE criteria are met.

distractorExplanations.b: Persistent depressive disorder requires depressed mood for most of two years in adults, not a three-week post-layoff episode.
distractorExplanations.c: Adjustment disorder is used when symptoms are marked but do not meet another full disorder; a complete MDE is coded as MDD even if a layoff occurred.
distractorExplanations.d: Cyclothymia needs at least two years of hypomanic and depressive symptoms that never meet full mania, hypomania, or MDE criteria.

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.prompt: A 29-year-old with two prior major depressive episodes now has five days of decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, spending sprees, and increased talkativeness. Work continues, though colleagues notice the change. No hospitalization or psychosis. Which conceptualization is most accurate?

options.a: Bipolar I disorder, because any elevated mood with spending automatically meets criteria for a manic episode
options.b: Bipolar II disorder if this is hypomania, given the duration, intact functioning, and documented MDE history
options.c: Cyclothymic disorder, because the mood elevation lasted less than seven days so bipolar diagnoses are closed
options.d: Major depression with mixed features only, because hypomania cannot be diagnosed unless psychosis is present

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.explanation: Hypomania is a distinct period of elevated, expansive, or irritable mood plus increased energy lasting at least four days, with symptoms observable by others, without marked impairment, hospitalization, or psychosis. Combined with at least one major depressive episode and no lifetime manic episode, that pattern is bipolar II. Mania, not hypomania, is defined by marked impairment, hospitalization, or psychotic features.

distractorExplanations.a: Spending is a symptom, not proof of mania; this episode lacks marked impairment, hospitalization, and psychosis required for bipolar I.
distractorExplanations.c: Hypomania's minimum duration is four days, not seven; seven days (or any duration if hospitalized) applies to mania.
distractorExplanations.d: Psychosis is incompatible with hypomania and would upgrade the episode toward mania; mixed features do not erase a hypomanic episode.

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.prompt: Eight weeks after a highway crash with threatened death, a client has nightmares, flashbacks, driving avoidance, persistent negative mood, and hypervigilance most days. Symptoms have lasted more than one month and impair work. Which diagnosis fits best?

options.a: Adjustment disorder, because symptoms followed a discrete event so trauma-related diagnoses are excluded
options.b: Acute stress disorder, because the crash occurred less than three months ago and nightmares are still present
options.c: PTSD, given qualifying trauma plus intrusion, avoidance, mood change, and arousal lasting over a month
options.d: Specific phobia of vehicles, because the avoidance is limited to driving and does not affect other settings

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.explanation: PTSD requires actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence (Criterion A) plus symptoms from all four clusters—intrusion, avoidance, negative alterations in cognitions/mood, and arousal—lasting more than one month with impairment. This crash is qualifying trauma, clusters are present, and eight weeks exceeds the one-month duration. Acute stress disorder covers three days to one month after the event.

distractorExplanations.a: Adjustment disorder is for stressors that do not meet Criterion A or when another trauma disorder's full criteria are not met.
distractorExplanations.b: Acute stress disorder ends at one month; at eight weeks with full clusters, the duration points to PTSD, not ASD.
distractorExplanations.d: Phobia does not capture nightmares, flashbacks, negative mood, and hyperarousal after threatened death; avoidance is only one cluster.

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.prompt: Nine days after a breakup, a 24-year-old makes frantic calls, threatens self-injury, and splits the therapist as all-good then all-bad. Friends say this is new. School, work, and earlier relationships were stable. What should the LCSW do diagnostically?

options.a: Diagnose borderline personality disorder now, because splitting and abandonment fear are pathognomonic in a crisis
options.b: Diagnose histrionic personality disorder, because the distress is interpersonal, dramatic, and attention-seeking this week
options.c: Diagnose antisocial personality disorder, because threats of self-injury count as rule-breaking that started in adolescence
options.d: Hold a personality-disorder diagnosis; one crisis week is not a long, inflexible pattern across contexts

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.explanation: Personality disorders require an enduring pattern of inner experience and behavior that is inflexible, pervasive across situations, stable over time, and typically traceable to adolescence or early adulthood, with clinically significant impairment. A nine-day breakup crisis, even with splitting and abandonment panic, is not that pattern when prior functioning was stable. Diagnose the current clinical syndrome and reassess personality only with longitudinal, cross-context data.

distractorExplanations.a: BPD needs a pervasive pattern (identity, relationships, impulsivity, affect) beginning by early adulthood, not a single crisis week.
distractorExplanations.b: Histrionic PD is a long-standing attention-seeking style, not a nine-day dramatic reaction to a breakup.
distractorExplanations.c: Antisocial PD requires a conduct-disorder history and a pattern of violating others' rights, not self-injury threats in a breakup.

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.prompt: A 46-year-old's first depressive syndrome began only during a four-month heavy-drinking binge. After five weeks of documented abstinence, mood, sleep, and interest have returned to baseline. There is no independent mood history. Which diagnosis is most consistent?

options.a: Substance-induced depressive disorder, with the mood syndrome tracking intoxication rather than an independent MDD
options.b: Major depressive disorder, because five symptoms for two weeks always override any alcohol timeline in the history
options.c: Persistent depressive disorder, because mood symptoms lasted longer than one month while the client was bingeing
options.d: Bipolar I disorder, because mood that improves after stopping alcohol is evidence of an unrecognized manic switch

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.explanation: Substance/medication-induced depressive disorder is used when a prominent mood disturbance develops during or soon after intoxication or withdrawal, the substance is capable of producing those symptoms, and the disturbance is not better explained by an independent depressive disorder. Here onset tracks the binge, there is no prior independent MDE, and the syndrome remits with sustained abstinence. The LCSW still screens suicide risk and coordinates medical/SUD care without treating this as primary MDD.

distractorExplanations.b: Duration and symptom count can be met during intoxication; an independent MDD needs a history not fully explained by the substance.
distractorExplanations.c: Persistent depressive disorder is a two-year (adult) independent course, not a binge-limited month of low mood.
distractorExplanations.d: Remission after stopping alcohol supports a substance-induced mood syndrome, not a manic episode or bipolar I.

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.prompt: A 22-year-old develops voices and paranoid delusions over three weeks after high-dose stimulant use. Symptoms fade within ten days of stopping the drug. No prodrome, negative symptoms, or six-month course. What is the soundest diagnostic stance?

options.a: Schizophrenia, because two psychotic symptoms were present for most of a month and family risk is irrelevant
options.b: Substance/medication-induced psychotic disorder after tox and medical rule-outs, not schizophrenia
options.c: Schizoaffective disorder, because any psychosis that later recedes is proof of a mood-psychosis hybrid
options.d: Delusional disorder, because paranoia was the most prominent complaint even while voices were present

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.explanation: Schizophrenia requires two or more characteristic symptoms, including hallucinations, delusions, or disorganization, with continuous signs for at least six months and a one-month active phase, after substances and medical conditions are ruled out. A three-week stimulant-linked psychosis that remits off the drug is coded as substance/medication-induced psychotic disorder once intoxication, withdrawal, and medical mimics are considered. Family history never substitutes for duration and rule-outs.

distractorExplanations.a: Schizophrenia's six-month duration and substance rule-out are not met by a three-week stimulant psychosis that remits off the drug.
distractorExplanations.c: Schizoaffective disorder needs an uninterrupted period of major mood episode plus psychosis, and delusions/hallucinations for two weeks without prominent mood symptoms—not brief drug-related psychosis.
distractorExplanations.d: Delusional disorder is non-bizarre delusions lasting a month without prominent hallucinations or a substance cause.

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.prompt: A 15-year-old becomes inattentive, jumpy, and unable to finish homework after moving in with a violent caregiver. Elementary records and teacher notes before age 12 showed average attention. Rating scales now look 'ADHD-positive.' What should the LCSW conclude?

options.a: ADHD, combined presentation, because current rating scales are sufficient without a developmental interview
options.b: ADHD, predominantly inattentive, because teen-onset school failure still meets the age-of-onset rule
options.c: Intellectual developmental disorder, because exposure to violence always lowers IQ enough to explain inattention
options.d: Do not rubber-stamp ADHD; late inattention after danger needs trauma history, not a stimulant-as-test approach

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.explanation: ADHD requires several inattentive or hyperactive-impulsive symptoms present before age 12, across settings, not better explained by another condition. New teen-onset inattention and hypervigilance after entering an unsafe home point toward trauma-related attention disruption, not a neurodevelopmental course. Rating scales and a stimulant trial do not separate hypervigilance from ADHD; the LCSW takes a developmental and trauma history and treats safety first.

distractorExplanations.a: Scales capture current inattention but cannot date onset or sort trauma hypervigilance from ADHD; history is required.
distractorExplanations.b: DSM-5-TR ADHD needs several symptoms before age 12; isolated teen-onset after danger fails that criterion.
distractorExplanations.c: Intellectual developmental disorder requires deficits in intellectual and adaptive functioning with developmental onset, not inferred from trauma alone.

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.prompt: A 33-year-old is hospitalized after eight days of almost no sleep, grandiose business plans, pressured speech, and reckless driving. Job and finances have collapsed. There is no substance intoxication on tox screen. Which episode type is this?

options.a: A manic episode consistent with bipolar I, given duration, marked impairment, and hospitalization
options.b: A hypomanic episode consistent with bipolar II, because irritability can occur without any psychotic features
options.c: Brief psychotic disorder, because hospital admission by itself defines brief psychosis rather than a mood episode
options.d: ADHD, adult presentation, because decreased need for sleep is always a childhood-onset attention problem

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.explanation: A manic episode is a week or more (or any duration if hospitalized) of elevated, expansive, or irritable mood and increased energy with symptoms such as grandiosity, decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, and risky behavior, plus marked impairment, hospitalization, or psychosis. Hospitalization and occupational collapse place this on the mania side, which defines bipolar I once substances and medical causes are excluded. Hypomania is explicitly not severe enough to cause marked impairment or hospital care.

distractorExplanations.b: Hypomania cannot include marked impairment or hospitalization; those features upgrade the episode to mania.
distractorExplanations.c: Brief psychotic disorder is psychosis lasting one day to one month without a full mood-episode picture; this is a mood episode with impairment.
distractorExplanations.d: ADHD sleep problems are not a week of no need for sleep with grandiosity, pressured speech, and hospital-level collapse.

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.prompt: Six weeks after a mutually agreed divorce, a 38-year-old has tearfulness, initial insomnia, and slipping deadlines. There was no threatened death or violence, no panic attacks, and symptoms fall short of a major depressive episode. Which diagnosis fits?

options.a: PTSD, because any life change that produces dreams about the marriage meets Criterion A trauma
options.b: Adjustment disorder, given a non-trauma stressor within three months and marked but subthreshold symptoms
options.c: Acute stress disorder, because symptoms started within three months of the divorce and include poor sleep
options.d: Persistent depressive disorder, because six weeks of low mood already meets the two-year adult duration rule

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.explanation: Adjustment disorder is a marked emotional or behavioral response to an identifiable stressor beginning within three months, out of proportion or impairing, that does not meet criteria for another mental disorder and is not normal bereavement. A divorce is a qualifying stressor but not Criterion A trauma, and this picture is not a full MDE, PTSD, or ASD. Symptoms typically resolve within six months after the stressor or its consequences end.

distractorExplanations.a: PTSD Criterion A requires actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence—not an agreed divorce.
distractorExplanations.c: Acute stress disorder follows Criterion A trauma and lasts three days to one month; a divorce is not that trauma exposure.
distractorExplanations.d: Persistent depressive disorder requires two years of depressed mood in adults, not six weeks of post-divorce distress.

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.prompt: A 27-year-old describes unwanted contamination images and spends two hours daily washing until the skin cracks, causing lateness. The client calls the rituals 'pointless' and wants them gone. Insight is fair. Which diagnosis is indicated?

options.a: Obsessive-compulsive personality disorder, because neatness and rule-following are a lifelong character style
options.b: Generalized anxiety disorder, because the worries last all day and concern possible illness or dirt
options.c: A primary psychotic delusion of contamination, because performing rituals proves that insight is absent
options.d: OCD, given time-consuming, impairing obsessions and/or compulsions experienced as intrusive and unwanted

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.explanation: OCD is marked by obsessions (intrusive, unwanted thoughts, images, or urges) and/or compulsions that are time-consuming (often more than one hour a day) or cause distress or impairment. Ego-dystonic contamination fears plus washing rituals with retained insight fit OCD. OCPD is an ego-syntonic perfectionistic personality pattern without true obsessions and compulsions; GAD worries everyday problems rather than ritualized neutralizing.

distractorExplanations.a: OCPD is a pervasive, ego-syntonic need for order and control, not two-hour ego-dystonic washing rituals the client wants to stop.
distractorExplanations.b: GAD involves difficult-to-control worries about several real-life domains, not neutralizing compulsions to an intrusive image.
distractorExplanations.c: Most people with OCD have some insight; rituals do not equal a fixed false belief held as psychotic delusion.

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.prompt: A 50-year-old develops fatigue, weight gain, slowed thinking, and low mood over four months without a psychosocial trigger. The LCSW is formulating before closing a primary depressive diagnosis. What is the priority rule-out step?

options.a: Screen medical mimics (thyroid, sleep apnea, substances) and coordinate evaluation before locking a primary mood diagnosis
options.b: Diagnose persistent depressive disorder immediately because a four-month low mood already equals a two-year course
options.c: Diagnose ADHD, inattentive presentation, because slowed thinking in midlife is a missed childhood neurodevelopmental marker
options.d: Diagnose narcissistic personality disorder because distress about appearance and energy is a long character pattern

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.explanation: Depressive and cognitive syndromes can be produced by medical conditions (for example hypothyroidism), sleep disorders such as obstructive sleep apnea, and substances. DSM-5-TR requires that the disturbance is not attributable to those effects before a primary depressive disorder is recorded. The LCSW does not prescribe or order labs independently where that is outside scope, but does screen, document rule-outs, and coordinate medical evaluation rather than closing MDD or PDD on interview alone.

distractorExplanations.b: Persistent depressive disorder needs two years in adults; four months is not that duration and skips medical mimics.
distractorExplanations.c: ADHD requires childhood-onset symptoms across settings; new midlife slowing with weight gain is a medical-rule-out picture.
distractorExplanations.d: Narcissistic PD is a long-standing grandiosity/need-for-admiration pattern, not a four-month energy and mood change.

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.prompt: A 31-year-old has recurrent unexpected panic attacks for two months and now skips workouts and coffee for fear of another attack. Attacks are not cued by a specific object or social situation. Which diagnosis is most accurate?

options.a: Specific phobia, because the person now avoids gyms and caffeinated drinks after noticing bodily sensations
options.b: Panic disorder, given recurrent unexpected attacks plus persistent worry or a maladaptive behavior change
options.c: PTSD, because autonomic arousal after an attack is the same as Criterion E hyperarousal after trauma
options.d: Somatic symptom disorder, because the bodily sensations of panic are medically unexplained by definition

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.explanation: Panic disorder requires recurrent unexpected panic attacks plus at least one month of persistent concern about additional attacks or their consequences, or a significant maladaptive change in behavior related to the attacks. Avoiding exercise and caffeine to prevent attacks is that behavior change. A panic attack is an event, not a diagnosis; unexpected attacks plus worry/avoidance make the disorder. Cued avoidance of a specific object is phobia, not this pattern.

distractorExplanations.a: Specific phobia is marked, cued fear of a circumscribed object or situation; here attacks were unexpected, then lifestyle changed to prevent them.
distractorExplanations.c: PTSD needs Criterion A trauma and four clusters; panic physiology without that trauma is not PTSD.
distractorExplanations.d: Panic symptoms are an autonomic surge, not a somatic symptom disorder, which centers on persistent distressing somatic complaints and related thoughts.

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.prompt: A 44-year-old has felt 'gray' most of the day, more days than not, for three years, with low energy and poor self-esteem, never meeting a full major depressive episode, and still working. Which diagnosis is most consistent?

options.a: Major depressive disorder, recurrent, because three years of sadness is automatically coded as severe MDD
options.b: Cyclothymic disorder, because chronic low mood in adults is treated as a mild bipolar spectrum default
options.c: Persistent depressive disorder, given two-plus years of depressed mood without a current full MDE
options.d: Adjustment disorder, chronic type, because adult mood problems always require an identified recent stressor

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.explanation: Persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia) is depressed mood for most of the day, more days than not, for at least two years in adults, plus at least two associated symptoms (for example low energy, poor self-esteem), without a break of two months or more. If a full MDE has not occurred, it is PDD without the specifier for intermittent MDE. Three years of subthreshold, stable low mood while working fits that course rather than recurrent MDD or cyclothymia.

distractorExplanations.a: MDD requires discrete major depressive episodes at full symptom count; chronic subthreshold mood is PDD, not automatic severe MDD.
distractorExplanations.b: Cyclothymia needs at least two years of hypomanic and depressive periods that never meet full mania, hypomania, or MDE—not unipolar gray mood.
distractorExplanations.d: Adjustment disorder begins within three months of a stressor and is not a three-year independent low-mood course.

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.prompt: A client meets full criteria for alcohol use disorder. Independently, a three-week major depressive episode began during a six-month sober period, with no intoxication or withdrawal at onset. How should comorbidity be handled?

options.a: Code only alcohol use disorder; any mood symptoms in a person with AUD are substance-induced by definition
options.b: Code only unspecified depressive disorder, because two diagnoses are never allowed on the same formulation
options.c: Drop the mood diagnosis if the client still attends mutual-help meetings, because recovery excludes MDD
options.d: Give both diagnoses when each disorder's full criteria are independently met

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.explanation: Comorbidity means two or more disorders are present, each meeting its own criteria. An MDE that begins during a sustained sober period is not explained by intoxication or withdrawal, so it is an independent depressive disorder alongside alcohol use disorder. Overlapping symptoms (sleep, concentration) are not double-coded as a second diagnosis unless the remaining picture still meets full criteria. Specifiers refine one diagnosis; they are not a second disorder.

distractorExplanations.a: Substance-induced depression requires onset during intoxication/withdrawal; an MDE in a six-month sober window is independent.
distractorExplanations.b: DSM-5-TR allows multiple diagnoses when each is justified; unspecified depression is for when full criteria are not met.
distractorExplanations.c: Mutual-help attendance is treatment, not a rule-out; recovery does not erase an independent MDE.

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.prompt: A 7-year-old has always had restricted interests, insistence on sameness, and social-communication delays at home and school. There is no trauma history. Teachers noted the pattern in preschool. Which diagnosis is most consistent?

options.a: PTSD, because rigidity after any change in routine is coded as a trauma-related avoidance cluster
options.b: Social anxiety disorder only, because the child is quiet with unfamiliar adults and prefers known caregivers
options.c: Autism spectrum disorder, given early social-communication differences and restricted, repetitive patterns
options.d: ADHD only, because any school impairment in a child is treated as attention-deficit until a stimulant trial

aswb-clinical-readiness-check-diagnosis-.explanation: Autism spectrum disorder is a neurodevelopmental condition with persistent deficits in social communication and interaction across contexts, plus restricted, repetitive patterns of behavior, interests, or activities, with onset in the early developmental period. Preschool-onset sameness, restricted interests, and social-communication delays without a trauma history fit ASD. Trauma-related inattention or freeze responses would have a post-event timeline; this course is developmental from early childhood.

distractorExplanations.a: PTSD requires a qualifying trauma and four symptom clusters; early-onset restricted interests without trauma are not PTSD.
distractorExplanations.b: Social anxiety is fear of scrutiny in social situations with typical social-communication skills; it does not explain lifelong restricted interests and sameness.
distractorExplanations.d: ADHD is inattention/hyperactivity beginning before age 12; it does not account for social-communication deficits and restricted, repetitive behaviors.
